name: el_parameters
description: The user-adjustable parameters of the electrical editor: the placement rules and their values in both rule sets, the snap radius, the symbol scale and room distance, the colours of the screen (black stage) and of the print (white paper), screen line widths, how the drawing is recoloured, the symbols of the generated examples. ONE home for each value: the Python tools, the page, the print view, the Documentation tab and the tests read them from here (vpt/el_params.py; vpt/el_rules.py and vpt/el_layout.py merge them into what they return). The page's Parameters panel shows, edits, copies, saves and loads this file (schema schema/el_parameters.schema.json). Every value says where it comes from; 'starting value – confirm' means we chose it and nobody has confirmed it.

snap.label: Snapping
snap.source: Our choice; the same for both rule sets.

snap_radius_m.label: Snap radius
snap_radius_m.note: Starting value – confirm. A symbol let go within this distance of a suggestion of its kind is placed exactly on the suggestion (and turned to its wall). Hold Alt/Option, or switch Snap off, to place freely. Our choice; the same for both rule sets.

symbol_scale.label: Symbol size factor
symbol_scale.note: Placed symbols are drawn at their nominal size in mm on the storey sheet (presets/el_symbols_at.json) times this factor. Starting value - confirm.

room_label_max_m.label: Room label within (no outline)
room_label_max_m.note: A symbol outside every room outline is given the nearest room label of a room WITHOUT an outline when that label is at most this far away (method 'nearest label'); else its room is could-not-tell. Starting value - confirm.

colours_screen.label: Colours on screen (black background)
colours_screen.source: Our choice for contrast on black: saturated, one hue per category. Every colour has at least 3:1 contrast against the background (WCAG 2.1 non-text contrast, 1.4.11), checked by the tests. No Austrian colour standard was checked (see standard_note).

connect_allowed.label: Connect: symbols the switch may control

colours_print.label: Colours in the print (white paper)
colours_print.source: Dark and saturated colours for paper, at least 3:1 against white (checked by the tests). No Austrian colour standard was checked (see standard_note).

marker_hit.label: Suggestion it would snap to (never printed)

drawing_screen.label: Drawing on screen (light on black)
drawing_screen.source: Our choice. Each CAD colour keeps its hue (so Bestand, Abbruch and Neubau stay apart by colour as in the CAD file) with less saturation; its lightness is turned round into the ranges below: dark lines become light, white fills become dark.

drawing_print.label: Drawing in the print (dark on white)
drawing_print.source: Our choice: the drawing printed in dark, muted colours so that the symbols stand out; hues kept (Bestand, Abbruch, Neubau stay apart), lightness kept in order.

screen_lines.label: Line widths and marker size on screen
screen_lines.source: Our choice. Screen pixels at every zoom (non-scaling strokes), so a line never gets thinner than this when the whole storey is shown. The print uses the mm widths of print_lines and of the symbol set.

dim_opacity.label: Connect: symbols the switch cannot control

print_lines.label: Link lines in the print
print_lines.source: Our choice: a thin dashed line on the A3 sheet, in mm on the storey sheet (scaled with the drawing).

examples.label: Examples (generated)
examples.source: Our choice of symbols for the generated examples (vpt/el_examples.py); positions come from the placement suggestions, never typed in.

simple_doors.label: Simple example: doors of its room

smoke_offset_m.label: Smoke alarm: beside the ceiling light

standard_note: No Austrian colour standard for the colours of installation-plan symbols was checked: these colours are starting values. Confirm them with the Elektroplaner and against the drawing conventions of ÖNORM A 6240 (to verify: its text was not available, so it is not known whether it sets colours for electrical installation plans).
contrast_min_note: WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.11 (non-text contrast): 3:1 for graphical objects. Every symbol, link, marker and selection colour of both palettes is checked against its palette's background by the tests.

rules.label: Placement rules
rules.note: Two rule sets with the same keys. A rule whose value is null gives no suggestion, and a layout check that needs it says 'could not tell: no value yet'. The suggestions are computed by vpt/el_rules.py when the plan file is exported (tools/export_plan.py): a changed geometry value takes effect on the page after the plan is exported again with this file.

rule_sets.name: starting values (to confirm)
rule_sets.note: Values we chose to get started. None is taken from a standard: each says where the idea comes from. Replace them with the Elektroplaner's values (the second set) once they are known.

rule_sets.name: Elektroplaner values
rule_sets.status: no values yet: to be provided by the Elektroplaner
rule_sets.note: Every value is null until the Elektroplaner gives one; fill in value and source here. While a value is null its rule gives no suggestion and its hint says 'no value yet'.

switch_from_frame_m.label: Switch: distance from the door frame
switch_from_frame_m.text: A switch or push-button is suggested beside each door of a room, on the room's side, on the handle side (the side opposite the hinge, from the door swing in the plan file), this far along the wall from the edge of the opening. The suggestion sits in the middle of the range.

switch_inset_m.label: Switch: into the room (swing side)
switch_inset_m.text: How far from the door's opening line (the chord of its swing arc, which lies on the wall face of the side the door opens into) the suggestion lies, on the side the door opens into.

switch_inset_other_m.label: Switch: into the room (other side)
switch_inset_other_m.text: The same on the other side of the door, where the wall's thickness lies between the opening line and the room (the plan file does not know the wall thickness).

socket_min_piece_m.label: Socket: shortest wall piece
socket_min_piece_m.text: A socket is suggested at the centre of every piece of the room's outline between its door openings; pieces shorter than this get none.

socket_inset_m.label: Socket: off the wall face
socket_inset_m.text: How far into the room from the outline (the wall face) the suggestion lies, so the symbol sits on the wall.

door_cut_max_m.label: Door opening cuts a wall piece within
door_cut_max_m.text: A door's or window's opening cuts a piece of the room's outline when the opening runs along it and lies at most this far from it (about one wall thickness). Used for sockets and kitchen outlets.

window_margin_m.label: Window: sockets keep clear by
window_margin_m.text: Socket and kitchen suggestions keep clear of each window opening (from the plan file) and of this much wall on both sides of it; a wall piece with a window is split there.

ceiling_light_at.label: Ceiling light: where
ceiling_light_at.text: A ceiling light is suggested at the room's centre: the centre of its outline, else (no outline, or the centre lies outside an L-shaped outline) the room label's point.

kitchen_keywords.label: Kitchen: label words
kitchen_keywords.text: A room whose label contains one of these words is a kitchen: kitchen and appliance outlets are suggested along its wall pieces.

kitchen_spacing_m.label: Kitchen outlets: spacing
kitchen_spacing_m.text: Kitchen and appliance outlets are suggested along each wall piece of a kitchen, this far apart.

kitchen_end_margin_m.label: Kitchen outlets: from the piece's ends
kitchen_end_margin_m.text: The first and last kitchen suggestion of a wall piece lie this far from its ends (doors, corners).

hint_switch_near_door_m.label: Check: a switch counts for a door within
hint_switch_near_door_m.text: Layout check H3 'door without a switch': a door of a room with a light counts as having a switch when a switch or push-button symbol lies within this distance of the door's opening.

room_words_living.label: Room type living: label words
room_words_living.text: A room whose label contains one of these words is a living room (layout checks). Kitchens and wet rooms are told first.

room_words_bedroom.label: Room type bedroom: label words
room_words_bedroom.text: A room whose label contains one of these words is a bedroom (layout checks).

room_words_hall.label: Room type hall: label words
room_words_hall.text: A room whose label contains one of these words is a hall or corridor (layout checks).

room_words_storage.label: Room type storage: label words
room_words_storage.text: A room whose label contains one of these words is a storeroom (layout checks): known, so its type is not 'could not tell'.

check_light_room_types.label: Check: rooms that need a light
check_light_room_types.text: Layout check: every room of these types has at least one light symbol (the room types: presets/el_rules_at.json checks.room_types).

check_min_sockets_living.label: Check: sockets in a living room, at least
check_min_sockets_living.text: Layout check: a living room has at least this many socket outlets (a double socket counts two).

check_min_sockets_bedroom.label: Check: sockets in a bedroom, at least
check_min_sockets_bedroom.text: Layout check: a bedroom has at least this many socket outlets.

check_min_sockets_kitchen.label: Check: sockets in a kitchen, at least
check_min_sockets_kitchen.text: Layout check: a kitchen has at least this many socket outlets, besides its appliance outlets.

check_min_sockets_wet.label: Check: sockets in a wet room, at least
check_min_sockets_wet.text: Layout check: a wet room (bath, WC) has at least this many socket outlets. Where in the room they may go (shower and bath zones) is not checked.

check_min_sockets_hall.label: Check: sockets in a hall, at least
check_min_sockets_hall.text: Layout check: a hall has at least this many socket outlets.

check_min_appliance_outlets_kitchen.label: Check: appliance outlets in a kitchen, at least
check_min_appliance_outlets_kitchen.text: Layout check: a kitchen has at least this many appliance outlets (the kitchen and appliance symbols), one of them a cooker outlet.

check_smoke_room_types.label: Check: rooms that need a smoke alarm
check_smoke_room_types.text: Layout check: every room of these types has a smoke alarm symbol.

switch_from_frame_m.source: Idea: on German and Austrian plans a light switch usually sits beside the door on the handle side, about a hand's width from the frame (the installation-zone convention known from German practice, DIN 18015-3). Not checked against that standard or against any Austrian rule.

switch_inset_m.source: Our choice, so that the symbol stands just inside the room on the plan; a drawing convenience, not from any standard.

switch_inset_other_m.source: Our guess: a typical inner wall (about 0.12 to 0.25 m) plus a little; not measured and not from any standard.

socket_min_piece_m.source: Our guess: shorter pieces are usually returns and niches. Not from any standard.

socket_inset_m.source: Our choice, so that the symbol sits on the wall on the plan; a drawing convenience, not from any standard.

door_cut_max_m.source: Our guess at a thick Altbau wall plus a margin; not measured.

window_margin_m.source: Our guess: room for the window reveal and a curtain; not measured and not from any standard.

ceiling_light_at.source: Idea: one ceiling outlet in the middle of the room is the usual default on plans; the Elektroplaner may plan more lights or another position.

kitchen_keywords.source: Our list of German and English words for a kitchen; check it against the room labels of the drawing.

kitchen_spacing_m.source: Idea: the usual kitchen cabinet module is 60 cm wide, so one outlet per module. Not from an electrical standard.

kitchen_end_margin_m.source: Idea: half a 60 cm cabinet module. Not from an electrical standard.

hint_switch_near_door_m.source: Our choice: a switch more than about an arm's length from the door is not 'at the door'. Not from any standard.

room_words_living.source: Our list of German and English words; check it against the room labels of the drawing.

room_words_bedroom.source: Our list of German and English words; check it against the room labels of the drawing.

room_words_hall.source: Our list of German and English words; check it against the room labels of the drawing.

room_words_storage.source: Our list of German and English words; check it against the room labels of the drawing.

check_light_room_types.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; most rooms of a flat get a ceiling outlet.

check_min_sockets_living.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; ÖVE and DIN guidance on numbers of outlets was not checked.

check_min_sockets_bedroom.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; ÖVE and DIN guidance on numbers of outlets was not checked.

check_min_sockets_kitchen.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; ÖVE and DIN guidance on numbers of outlets was not checked.

check_min_sockets_wet.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; ÖVE and DIN guidance on numbers of outlets was not checked.

check_min_sockets_hall.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; ÖVE and DIN guidance on numbers of outlets was not checked.

check_min_appliance_outlets_kitchen.source: Our starting value, not from a standard: a cooker and a dishwasher.

check_smoke_room_types.source: Our starting value, not from a standard; the Austrian rules on smoke alarms (building regulations, OIB guidelines) were not checked.
